question: What is the primary purpose of food budgeting in dietetics?

options.A: Balancing financial resources with nutritional requirements
options.B: Reducing weekly grocery trips to exactly one
options.C: Maximizing the purchase of imported food items
options.D: Eliminating all processed foods from the household

explanation: Food budgeting specifically aims to manage financial resources so that necessary nutrients are obtained without causing financial distress. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h1)

question: Why do standard meal plans often fail for low-income clients?

options.A: They focus exclusively on micronutrients rather than calories
options.B: They are too complex to prepare without professional training
options.C: They frequently require expensive or inaccessible ingredients
options.D: They forbid the consumption of local agricultural products

explanation: Standard meal plans often assume unlimited resources, recommending items that strain a limited household budget. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h1)

question: Which nutrient deficiencies are most commonly associated with resource-constrained households?

options.A: Protein, iron, calcium, and vitamin A
options.C: Complex sugars and trans fatty acids
options.D: Vitamin C, potassium, and dietary fiber

explanation: Limited budgets often restrict access to diverse foods rich in essential proteins, iron, calcium, and certain vitamins. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h2)

question: How should a nurse prioritize food choices when working with a restricted budget?

options.A: Eliminating all forms of protein to save money
options.C: Focusing on nutrient-dense staples over empty calories

explanation: Nutrient-dense foods provide essential vitamins and minerals per calorie, maximizing nutritional value for limited financial outlay. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h2)

question: What is a primary benefit of structuring a weekly meal plan?

options.B: Ensuring every meal contains imported ingredients
options.C: Preventing impulsive purchases and reducing food spoilage
options.D: Eliminating the need to ever cook fresh meals

explanation: Planning meals ahead of time guides targeted shopping lists, minimizing unplanned buys and expired ingredients. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h3)

question: A patient asks how batch cooking saves money. What is the best response?

options.A: It allows food to be stored indefinitely without refrigeration
options.B: It automatically doubles the protein content of grains
options.C: It completely removes the need to buy fresh vegetables
options.D: It reduces energy consumption and minimizes ingredient waste

explanation: Cooking larger quantities at once optimizes fuel usage and utilizes bulk ingredients efficiently before they spoil. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h3)

question: What is the main advantage of purchasing staple items in bulk?

options.B: Extended shelf life for fresh produce
options.C: Lower unit cost for non-perishable goods

explanation: Buying in larger quantities usually decreases the price paid per individual unit, stretching the household budget. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h4)

question: Why should shoppers compare unit prices instead of total package prices?

options.A: It indicates whether the food was produced locally or imported
options.B: It shows the exact vitamin content per serving of the food
options.C: It reveals the true relative cost of the product regardless of package size
options.D: It determines the total cooking time required for the item

explanation: Unit pricing breaks down costs into standard measurements, allowing accurate comparison between different brands and package sizes. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h4)

question: What does discarding food primarily represent in the context of household management?

options.A: An effective method for reducing kitchen labor
options.B: A direct loss of financial capital and nutritional value
options.C: An essential step in maintaining household hygiene
options.D: A legal requirement for expired packaged goods

explanation: Throwing away edible food wastes the money spent acquiring it and the nutrients it could have provided. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h5)

question: Which practice is most effective for managing surplus cooked food safely?

options.A: Reheating the entire batch of food before every meal
options.B: Rapidly cooling and storing leftovers in airtight containers
options.C: Mixing new groceries directly into old uncooled leftovers
options.D: Leaving cooked food uncovered on the counter overnight

explanation: Proper cooling and airtight storage inhibit bacterial growth, ensuring leftovers remain safe for consumption. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h5)

question: Which Nigerian food item is an exceptionally rich, low-cost source of plant-based protein?
explanation: Cowpeas are widely available, affordable, and provide significant amounts of plant protein and fiber. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h6)

question: Why are local green leafy vegetables like fluted pumpkin leaves emphasized in budget nutrition counseling?

options.A: They require no washing or preparation before cooking
options.B: They can be stored at room temperature for several months
options.C: They completely replace the need for carbohydrate intake
options.D: They are economical sources of essential minerals and vitamins

explanation: Local greens are nutrient-dense, affordable, and rich in micronutrients like iron and calcium. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h6)

question: What is a key requirement for effective financial nutrition counseling?

options.A: Insistence on purchasing premium organic produce
options.B: Avoiding any discussion of household income
options.C: Strict enforcement of imported dietary guidelines

explanation: Counseling must respect the client's cultural background and financial limits to achieve sustainable dietary changes. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h7)

question: What is NOT a recommended approach when counseling a client on food budgeting?

options.A: Setting small, achievable dietary adjustment goals
options.B: Reviewing current household spending habits together
options.C: Collaborating to identify affordable cultural food alternatives
options.D: Imposing rigid dietary standards that ignore financial reality

explanation: Imposing unrealistic standards leads to client frustration and non-adherence; counseling must be tailored to actual financial capacities. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h7)
